location: Malmstrom AFB RAPCON, Montana (author personal observation)
description: Author (16/17 yrs, janitor at Malmstrom tower) shown five unidentified radar 'targets' by FAA controller; two jets launched. Third-hand report from father: UFOs near Minuteman sites in Judith Basin ascended vertically at enormous speed.
Repeated sightings of 'unexplained phenomena' near AEC installation by OSI agents, airline & military pilots, security inspectors, citizens (FBI memo 1949-01-31). Another on 6 Jan 1949.
Dr. Lincoln La Paz sights green fireball crossing Los Alamos reservation; second fireball 8 days later seen by AEC security agent.
No fewer than 14 separate UFO sightings reported by security officers, military pilots and radar personnel.
Silvery disc hovering over plant seen by Hanford personnel; tracked on radar at Moses Lake; F-82 scrambled; object left at high speed. Public Air Force explanation: conventional aircraft.
Army Memo For Record (Maj. U.G. Carlan, from Lt Col Mildren): round objects above 15,000 ft; jet intercept attempts negative.
Four non-scheduled airline pilots (Baldwin, Robertson, Shenkel, Summers) reported saucer hovering near AEC plant (Miami Herald). Ruppelt later attributed to Skyhook balloon; Hastings doubts.
F-94 crew at 26,000 ft sees large round white object with dim reddish 'windows', radar lock-on, object reverses/dives; collision seemed imminent (Ruppelt).
Four DuPont employees saw four ~15-inch yellow/gold disks approaching '400 Area'; two more later; one rose to clear tanks (FBI letter Hoover to AFOSI/IG 1952-05-15).
John A. Anderson & ~100 engineers watched greenish object darting erratically ~2 min (McDonald 1968 House testimony; date uncertain).

Flares/lights observed by guards: 6 & 8 Mar, 17 Mar (7 sightings, triangulated, Capt. Horace McCullough), 16 & 18 Apr; 27 Apr tiny ping-pong-ball lights within 6 ft of guards; 28 Apr 12 guards in 9 sightings. Army: objects 'bracketed' nuclear weapons area.
Conference of 4th Army, AFOSI, ONI, CIC, FBI, AFSWP: Army & Navy 'grave concern'; AFSWP: natural phenomena.

Series: 6 Dec 1948 green fireball (Toulouse); 6 Jan 1949 diamond-shaped object at Ordnance Area (OSI SA Boling); 17 Feb 1949 fireball + cigar-shaped light seen by ~100 people (SA Neef); 13 Mar 1949; 27 Nov 1949 fireball (W.W. Jones, Lt Col Lancaster); 21 Mar 1950 multiple UFOs (10 OSI Spot Intel Reports); 24 Mar 1950 MPs saw objects.

location: Nevada Proving Ground (Yucca Flat), Buster-Jangle Charlie
description: Anonymous 'Mr. M.' (USAF airman from Nellis, sentry duty) reports 18 silvery domed discs in formation hovering 30-60 sec ~15-20 min before 14-kt Charlie shot; Sgt of the Guard said 'If we're smart, we won't say anything.' Walter Webb interviewed 1981 (phone), dated it by yield/sunrise.
Veteran Bernard Clark reports many unidentified airborne objects glinting at daybreak; Hastings judges likely sun glint off sampling/photo aircraft/B-50.
F-86 pilots Capt. Howard F. Paulin and 2nd Lt. Lester F. Page report green flare descending at 26,000 ft, ~26 h after Ranger Baker-1 debris cloud passed Albany; Blue Book: inconclusive.
American Airlines DC-4 crew sees bright green projectile-shaped object pass at 4,500 ft and explode into red fireballs ~23 h after Buster Dog; debris cloud map shows Texas coverage (Keyhoe).
Arizona Daily Star (3 Nov) 'Eerie Blue Flash Streaks Across Southwestern Skies', 9:05 pm MST, ~37 h after Dog.

location: Loring AFB, Maine (42nd Bomb Wing flight line)
description: 'John Smith' (42nd FMS jet mechanic) reports UFO hovering ~2-5 min over flight line as two Chrome Dome B-52s returned; large emergency turnout incl. many colonels; no aircraft damage; no discussion afterwards by witnesses (amnesia-like). Hastings dates it to Cuban Missile Crisis because tandem Chrome Dome sorties flew only then.

location: Echo Flight, Malmstrom AFB, MT (341st SMW)
description: All 10 Minuteman I missiles went No-Go ~0830 due to guidance & control faults; UFOs reportedly seen by maintenance teams at two widely separated LFs and confirmed by Security Alert Team before dawn. Official wing history: UFO rumors 'disproven'. Boeing investigators duplicated faults by injecting 'noise' into logic coupler; source unknown.

location: Oscar Flight (LCF Oscar), Malmstrom AFB, MT
description: Salas/Meiwald: guards report glowing red saucer hovering at LCF front gate; guard injured approaching; then 6-8 missiles go No-Go at once, mostly G&C. OSI debrief, NDAs signed, alert logs confiscated. Air Force records do not acknowledge the incident.
Airman James Ortyl and A2C Robert Pounders saw shimmering reddish-orange object pass within ~30 yds of dispatch office window; unreported.
Trucker Ken Williams reports dome-shaped bright object landing in ravine; Cascade County deputies notified Malmstrom; Great Falls Tribune coverage; declassified AF telex confirms notification.
Round white object circled a missile silo for prolonged periods; personnel told it was secret test vehicle (Fowler, from civilian employee).
SSgt Louis D. Kenneweg (341st MIMS) saw zigzagging light looming over flight line while driving to work.

date_text: 1964-09 (candidate dates 2, 3, 15 Sept per Jacobs log; Hastings favors 15 Sept 1964)
location: Big Sur, CA telescope site / Vandenberg AFB (Atlas D RV test) / Pacific
description: Lt. Bob Jacobs (1369th Photo Sqn, OIC Photo Instrumentation) says Image Orthicon telescope film of Atlas ICBM re-entry vehicle test showed domed disc UFO circle the dummy warhead, emit four flashes, warhead tumbled and fell hundreds of miles short of Eniwetok; film shown once or thrice at Vandenberg, then confiscated by 'agents'.
Harlowton Times (20 Feb 1975): 3 deputies see 3 UFOs; 0200 Air Policemen at K-1 report object hovering over K-10, 7 mi N of Harlowton airport.

location: Malmstrom AFB ICBM field (M-1, L-1, L-3, L-5, L-6, K-1, K-4, LIMA, Harlowton LCF), MT
description: 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's log: SAT/LCF crews report red/orange/yellow objects, objects 'issuing a black tubular object', height radar picks up 2-7 objects at 10-13,000 ft, J330 stationary then 7 kt at 12,000 ft; two F-106s scrambled from Great Falls; lights extinguish when fighters approach and return when they leave; 9 Nov 'orange white disc object'.
Bright star-like object passed over radar station at 1,000-2,000 ft, no noise (NORAD log 1125Z).
Documented incursion at Weapons Storage Area (per author; documents in Ch 18-onward).

location: Freezeout Lake, ~40 mi WNW of Malmstrom (B-52 practice runs)
description: Montana Fish & Game employee saw small round white light behind B-52, appearing to attach to it; bomber radar reportedly malfunctioned (Cascade Co. Sheriff Capt. Keith Wolverton; AF denied knowledge).

location: Malmstrom missile field / Loring WSA (SAC HQ daily recap)
description: Col. John W. Haley III recalls SAC daily report describing UFO hovering over Loring WSA (thought to be taking radiation readings) and UFO following a Malmstrom missile crew; F-106 intercepts from Minot (Hastings: no documentation of Minot launches; Great Falls fighters used).

location: Titan II complex 570-1, near Oracle AZ (570th SMS, Davis-Monthan AFB)
description: APRO (Lorenzens, 1969): brilliant light descending over site at midnight; two jets scrambled; object left north, returned minutes later; 3 anonymous witnesses. Hastings notes site was not yet operational on that date (no missile until 8 Dec 1962), so witnesses likely contractors.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, WY (90th SMW): LCFs Echo, Golf, Quebec; LFs B-4, E-2, G-1, H-2
description: Blue Book OOD Lt. Anspaugh logged calls from base commander (Col. Johnson), command post (Capt. Snelling), Sioux Army Depot CO etc. reporting circular colored silent object; explained by Air Force as twinkling stars (per Ch.16 ref at line 13056).

location: RAF Woodbridge / Rendlesham Forest / RAF Bentwaters, Suffolk, UK
description: Halt memo 'Unexplained Lights' (13 Jan 1981): triangular object in forest; depressions 1.5 in deep, 7 in dia; radiation 0.1 mR; star-like objects; beams of light. Hastings: dates in memo misstated; actual 26 Dec ~0300 and night of 27/28 Dec.

Unidentified security personnel reported luminous object hovering above WSA that sent laser-like beams down near/onto bunkers; Halt only heard radio chatter (he was in the forest) and saw beams elsewhere on base.
Civilian UFO sightings in local newspapers within days of first Atlas-Ds going on alert (book ref 1).

location: Walker AFB, NM - 579th SMS Atlas Site 9 (west of Roswell)
description: Repeated (3-10) occasions of silent objects hovering over silo and shining lights; guards frightened (Nelson DMCCC from launch capsule, did not see). Goss (guard) saw erratic fast lights twice, 2-3 weeks apart, winter 1963-64; told by launch commander they were military aircraft (once per SAC HQ duty officer).

location: Walker AFB Atlas Site 9 perimeter fence
description: Missile facilities technician Bob Caplan and guard approached ~6-inch flat circular yellowish light on ground outside fence; vanished when flashlights shone on it, reappeared 20-30 ft away. Caplan later interviewed by Walker AFOSI.

Fast-moving, erratic star-like light seen by many; Caplan later told by 6th Combat Defense Sq member it was tracked on radar and jets chased (hearsay; fighters presumably from Holloman). Kaminski: ~half his barracks watched 2-5 star-like lights for ~15 min doing 90-degree turns, no sonic booms.

location: Atlas site NE of Walker AFB
description: A1C Tom Kaminski (topside): two 'star' lights moving in unison; base told capsule radar had them and fighters were sent; next morning debrief: 'What UFOs? We didn't send up any fighters.'

location: Walker AFB Atlas Sites 6, 7, 8 (SSE of Roswell)
description: Lt Philip Moore (DMCCC at Site 7): crew at Sites 6/8 reported UFO hovering and rapidly shuttling; Site 7 crew (TSgt Jack Nevins, A1C Garner, A1C Rundag, Maj Dan Gilbert) saw silent light. Nevins: 'I cannot say I saw a UFO, only a light in the sky'; night crystal clear. No equipment effects; no debrief.

location: Walker AFB Atlas Site 8 (Route 285 south of Roswell) and other sites
description: A2C Barry Krause's letter to NICAP: frequent sightings, guards afraid; EPT saw weird light, capsule commander called SAC CP; SAC said KC-135 in area; object shot out of sight after tanker flew over; a Lt Col allegedly told to keep quiet; incident reports 'top secret'.

location: F.E. Warren AFB Atlas Site 1 (564th SMS)
description: MSgt Harold Renninger (then SSgt) and perimeter guard saw extremely bright silent light above dirt landing strip for 2-3 min; guard said Helio Courier; Renninger doubts. Other later lights near site (helicopters? spotlights?).

location: F.E. Warren AFB Site 1 Pad 1 (566th SMS area)
description: A1C Arthur McEnaney and guards saw round bright object hovering ~midnight; interceptors from Denver reportedly said weather balloon; told to keep quiet by SSgt Fred Coffer (national security).

location: FAA/Air Force SAGE building, Malmstrom AFB
description: Grover Austad (FAA controller, SAGE bldg): object tracked ~2,400 mph, zigzagged hundreds of miles; ADC controller confirmed seeing it; logged by FAA and reported to ADC (no feedback).

location: Salt Lake ATC Center / Burley, Idaho / Hill AFB
description: Austad: caller reports huge cigar-shaped object 60-70 mi N of Burley; F-80 from Hill AFB scrambled; pilot reportedly said 21 disc-shaped craft came out; object ~80,000 ft above pilot's ceiling.

Keyhoe (Flying Saucer Conspiracy): blinding glow over AEC test station at 12:40 am; witnesses Kelly Brooks and A.L. Taylor; Idaho Falls Post Register and AP reported; several earlier 'flash-bulb' lights.

Paul Selley: five unknown targets crossed scope very fast (no hover, no scramble recalled); several tracking events at night 7-11 pm; objects 'thousands of mph'. Hastings determines this was not the March 1967 event he saw (those five were stationary and fighters launched).

O.P. 'Pote' Morrow (RAPCON supervisor 1967-80) recalls fighters vectored southwest to unknown targets, nothing found; Kittleson: unknowns tracked near Lewistown and closer to Great Falls, aircraft scrambled from Great Falls; Weinzetl: ~1,700 mph high-altitude target ~20 s with Jerry Webster.

location: Minot AFB, Echo LCC (91st SMW), flights Alpha through Oscar
description: Lt David H. Schuur (DMCCC, Echo capsule) says a single bright object moved flight by flight (Alpha->Oscar, SE to NW) reported over PAS; Echo capsule received spurious indications incl. 'Launch in Progress' on several missiles, forced use of Inhibit switch; reset in minutes; logs/tapes collected, 'nothing happened' order; no OSI debrief.

location: F.E. Warren AFB, India Flight LCC area
description: Capt Larry Johnson (MCCC): light low to ground silently moved from LCC to LCC; SAT chased 10-15 min but could not close; not helicopter/airplane; no missile effects; no OSI debrief.

location: Minot AFB, ND: LFs O-6, N-7, Oscar/November LCFs, Bowbells area; B-52 inbound (5th BW)
description: Camper/maintenance teams and Base Ops log report bright maneuvering object near N-7; weather radar tracks object near Bowbells; B-52 radar paced by return 'as big or bigger than a KC-135' for ~20 mi, UHF transmitters disrupted; radarscope camera 14 frames; B-52 directed over ground-hovering oval orange object with tube and crescent; Blue Book case 12,548.

Larry Manross (launch crew commander 1966-70 per post) says UFOs were so frequent guards put chairs in front of LCFs to watch; one night an object 'buzzed' the LCF; radar tracked it; no report requested.
